text: Men are secondary gender, let me explain. From evolutionary and biological standpoint, men and women are not equal. Women are base of the species, while men are axillary, supportive and supplementary, secondary gender. All animal species that have sexual reproduction are complex organisms whose survival depends on adapting to changes in the environment. And those changes occur in the Y-chromosome. All genetical mutations arise in men through Y-chromosome. Women are the opposite, more stable and fundamental gender. Nature needs men for experiments, but women are needed for creation, rise and education of future generations of human species and also for leaderships. So the lady in the video says that from an evolutionary and biological standpoint, men are the secondary gender, auxiliary, supplementary, that nature only needs men for experiments and women are the real base of the species. Let's check if there's any truth to that. But before I go into details, let me be upfront about one thing. I'm not a biologist, so a lot of things I will be saying are coming from a research, so I might not be fully accurate in certain places, but I will try my best. So to be fair, her presented idea is not completely random. It sounds very similar to a theory from the Soviet biologist Vygen Geodakyan, who in the 1960s proposed what is called the evolutionary theory of sex. Very simplified, the idea is this. Females are the more stable, conservative part of the species, while males are the more variable experimental part. Nature supposedly tests changes more through males and then useful adaptations can spread through the population. So yes, there is a real theory behind some of this. But there are two problems. First, this is not mainstream biology in the way she presents it. Second, even if you discuss the theory seriously, it doesn't mean men are secondary. In biology, male and female are not defined by who is more important, more valuable, or more spiritually connected to the universe. They are usually defined by gametes. Females produce eggs, males produce sperm. And the moment she says that evolution happens through the Y chromosome, the whole thing starts falling apart. Because adaptation does not happen only through the Y chromosome. Human beings have the whole genome. Most genetic variation, most mutations, most inherited traits, and most diseases do not sit there patiently waiting inside the Y chromosome like it's a headquarters of evolution. Also, not every species even has a Y chromosome. Birds, for example, do not use the same XXXY system as humans. Some reptiles can have sex determined by temperature. So if your grand theory of life depends on the Y chromosome, it already has problems the moment a chicken enters the conversation. Now, there is one real point hidden inside the mess. Men do tend to show more variation in some traits. Males also contribute more new mutations to children on average, especially as fathers get older. But that mostly has to do with sperm production and cell division over time. It doesn't mean men are disposable side characters created by nature for beta testing. Nature is not sitting there saying, let's experiment on men and once we are done, we will upload the final version to women. And then comes the biggest jump. She says women are needed for creation, raising children, education, and leadership. Wait, leadership? Where did that come from? You can maybe make an argument about pregnancy, childbirth, and early child development. Fine, that is biology. But jumping from that to therefore women are biologically meant for leadership is not a scientific conclusion. That is just a political slogan that took a shortcut through a biology textbook. So the fair answer is this. Men are not secondary. Women are not secondary either. In sexual reproduction, both sexes are necessary.
